domain_label: Study System — Engagement, Gamification & Progress Visuals (owner calendar spec as product truth)
purpose: A method for turning the owner's concrete calendar-of-day-boxes brief into an enforceable progress-visual spec: per-day boxes that start white, fill like a green download bar as the day's tasks complete, show a tick only at true 100% and otherwise a percentage in 5% increments (the 21-state data model with floor-rounding), rendered in week and month views, plus a distinct course-level progress %, and grounded against prior art (GitHub contribution heatmap, Anki review heatmap, progress bars) and the engagement psychology (goal-gradient effect, habit formation, streaks, and the overjustification/streak-anxiety guardrails) — documenting the owner's requirement faithfully, tagging every claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, and never inventing a statistic the research file did not verify.
assumptions: no live product analytics or A/B result is supplied; every design recommendation is a heuristic prior grounded in the cited research file, not a measured outcome for this system

the owner's brief in OWNER_BRIEF.md is binding product truth to document faithfully, not a proposal to redesign; open points the owner did not specify are held as [UNKNOWN] or a tagged [ESTIMATE] recommendation, not invented as fact
vendor engagement statistics (e.g. Duolingo's 7-day-streak 2.4x figure) are carried as the vendor's own claim, never as independent evidence

several primary sources returned HTTP 403 this session (docs.github.com, blog.duolingo.com, ankiweb.net, ets.org); claims from those are graded [FACT - via search snippet] (weaker than a direct fetch) and the day-box rounding direction and past-day policy remain owner-unresolved
the day-view metric (effort = % of that day's assigned tasks done) and the course-view metric (mastery = units mastered / total) are different quantities and are never conflated into one number
exclusions: the multimodal spoken-answer capture pipeline (record -> queue -> batch transcribe -> LLM-grade), Whisper/whisper.cpp/faster-whisper and cloud-STT selection, and voice-note privacy (EDPB Article 9, OpenAI retention) belong to the multimodal-capture specialist (Part B of the research file) and are not modelled here
the scheduler / spaced-repetition backlog algorithm itself (how the day's task queue is generated) beyond consuming its output as the day-box denominator
the learner/mastery model internals that produce the course-level mastery state beyond reusing its output as the course-progress numerator
concrete visual styling (exact hex greens, pixel sizes, font, animation curves) beyond the owner-specified white-empty / green-fill / tick / 5%-numeral semantics
inventing engagement uplift numbers, pass rates, or retention figures the research file did not verify

glossary.definition: One square per calendar day, the owner's specified unit of the progress visual: it starts white (empty) with the day number shown in it, fills like a green downloading bar as that day's tasks/revision complete, shows a tick at 100%, and otherwise shows the completion percentage in 5% increments. [FACT - owner brief]

The derived per-day render state set: 20 floored partial percentages (0, 5, 10, ..., 95) plus the terminal tick = 21 possible states, computed as pct = floor((tasks_done/tasks_total)*20)*5 with the tick reserved for tasks_done == tasks_total. [ESTIMATE - design, from the owner's verbatim 5%-increment + tick spec]

The rule that the displayed percentage is rounded DOWN to the nearest 5% (67% -> 65), so no partially-complete day can ever show '100' or the tick; recommended (owner did not fix the direction) because the tick is the owner's distinguished terminal state. [ESTIMATE - medium-high confidence]

The checkmark that overlays/replaces the green fill only when the day's tasks are truly all done (done == total); it is the owner's single distinguished 'complete' state and the reason rounding must floor rather than round-to-nearest.

The rule that the day-box measures EFFORT (% of that day's assigned tasks done, a defined daily denominator) while the course view measures MASTERY (units mastered / total, from the learner model); they are different metrics and must be displayed separately, never merged into one number. [ESTIMATE - design]

Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng (2006), 'The Goal-Gradient Hypothesis Resurrected,' Journal of Marketing Research 43(1):39-58: people accelerate effort the closer they are to a reward, and even illusionary progress (a 12-stamp card with 2 pre-stamped) accelerates it; applied here, a visible partial fill in 5% steps strengthens the pull to finish today's tasks. [FACT]

GitHub's profile graph: a year of day-squares coloured by contribution count, split into 4 green intensity quartiles that recalibrate as the rolling window moves. It encodes RELATIVE volume by colour; the owner's design instead encodes ABSOLUTE completion by fill height + numeral because each day has a defined denominator. [FACT - via search snippet; official doc host 403 this session]

Duolingo's mechanic: a streak counts consecutive days with at least one lesson and resets to zero on a missed day unless a streak freeze was equipped in advance (bought beforehand, consumed one per miss, never retroactive). Duolingo frames it via loss aversion and claims a 7-day streak makes a learner 2.4x more likely to continue (vendor's own number). [FACT - via search snippet]

The guardrail distinction from Deci/Koestner/Ryan (1999) and Lepper (1973): progress visuals that INFORM the learner about their progress are treated far more favourably than expected tangible rewards, which can undermine intrinsic motivation; so the system keeps the fill/tick/percent as feedback and avoids adding points/prizes for studying. [FACT for the studies; ESTIMATE for the application]

nodes.definition: Enforce that the day-view and course-view measure different things and must not be conflated [ESTIMATE - design, high confidence]. The day-box measures EFFORT: the fraction of that day's assigned tasks done, with a defined daily denominator. The course view measures MASTERY: units mastered / total, from the learner model. nodes.definition: Ground why a visible partial fill should increase the pull to finish the day in the goal-gradient effect. nodes.definition: Model an optional streak mechanic on the calendar, grounded in Duolingo's design [FACT - via search snippet; blog.duolingo.com 403]. nodes.definition: Build the guardrail that keeps the progress visuals from undermining intrinsic motivation. Lepper, Greene & Nisbett (1973), JPSP 28(1):129-137 [FACT]: children promised an extrinsic reward for an activity they already enjoyed showed reduced subsequent intrinsic interest; unexpected rewards did not cause the drop. Deci, Koestner & Ryan (1999), a meta-analysis of 128 experiments, Psychological Bulletin 125(6):627-668 [FACT]: expected tangible rewards significantly undermined free-choice intrinsic motivation (engagement-contingent d = -0.40, completion-contingent d = -0.36, performance-contingent d = -0.28). Guardrail [ESTIMATE - application, high confidence]: keep the fill, tick and percentage as INFORMATIONAL FEEDBACK on progress — which the same literature treats far more favourably than tangible rewards — rather than adding points/prizes/currency for studying. The green fill and tick inform; they must not become a paid-out reward economy.

conflict_axes.description: Plotting future scheduled load aids planning, but a forecast fill risks being mistaken for actual completion and corrupting the tick's meaning.
poles: protect the meaning of actual completion
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: render forecast state in a clearly distinct style that can never show the tick, keeping solid green + tick reserved for actual completion

conflict_axes.name: owner_fidelity_vs_designer_improvement
conflict_axes.description: The owner specified concrete semantics to preserve, while designers may be tempted to improve or generalize them.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the brief as binding product truth; only resolve genuinely unspecified points, and record those as build-time decisions rather than silent redesigns

edge_cases.description: A day has zero assigned tasks (tasks_total == 0)
edge_cases.trigger: the scheduler assigns no tasks to a day or a rest day is created
edge_cases.mitigation: treat tasks_total==0 as an explicit empty/neutral state rather than dividing by zero, and decide (build-time) whether such a day counts toward or is skipped by the streak

edge_cases.description: A day at 96-99% completion is rounded to 100 and shows a false tick before the last task is done
edge_cases.trigger: round-to-nearest or round-up is used instead of floor
edge_cases.mitigation: floor to the 5% grid so the top partial is 95 and both '100' and the tick require done==total; add a test asserting done<total never yields complete

edge_cases.description: The percentage numeral and the green fill height disagree on the same box
edge_cases.trigger: the numeral and the fill are computed from separate calculations instead of the one model pct
edge_cases.mitigation: drive both encodings from the single model pct value so they cannot diverge

edge_cases.description: Day effort is summed or averaged into the course-level percentage
edge_cases.trigger: a UI or computation mixes task-completion into the mastery metric
edge_cases.mitigation: compute the two metrics from disjoint inputs, label them distinctly, and test that changing one does not move the other

edge_cases.description: A long streak is hard-reset to zero after a single missed day and the learner quits
edge_cases.trigger: the streak has no freeze/repair and a day is missed
edge_cases.mitigation: offer a pre-equipped freeze/repair, show a secondary long-horizon metric a single miss cannot zero, and keep the backlog non-punitive

edge_cases.description: A points/prizes reward economy is bolted onto studying and undermines intrinsic motivation
edge_cases.trigger: a gamification proposal adds tangible rewards for completing tasks
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the guardrail posture: keep visuals informational feedback only and reject added points/prizes/currency for studying

edge_cases.description: A forecast future-day box is mistaken for an already-completed day
edge_cases.trigger: forecast load is rendered in the same solid green as actual completion
edge_cases.mitigation: render forecast state in a clearly distinct style (e.g. outline/estimate) that can never show the tick

edge_cases.description: The same past incomplete day looks different in the week view than in the month view
edge_cases.trigger: the past-day freeze/gray policy is applied inconsistently across views
edge_cases.mitigation: choose one past-day policy at build time and apply it identically across both views

edge_cases.description: The 5%-step numeral is illegible in a dense month grid
edge_cases.trigger: the month view shrinks day cells below the numeral's legible size
edge_cases.mitigation: let the fill height carry the glance in the month view and reveal the numeral on inspection/hover, keeping semantics identical

edge_cases.description: GitHub's relative-colour quartile scale is copied into the study calendar
edge_cases.trigger: an engineer defaults to the familiar contribution-graph colour encoding
edge_cases.mitigation: use the owner's absolute fill-height completion because each study day has a defined denominator; reserve relative colour for a true volume view only if ever requested

edge_cases.description: An owner-unresolved point (rounding direction, past-day, weighting) is presented as the owner's requirement
edge_cases.trigger: a recommended default is written into the spec without flagging it as a build-time decision
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the three open points explicitly marked as build-time decisions with their tagged recommendations, never as stated owner intent

edge_cases.description: The tick is rendered from a loosely-computed pct==100 rather than the model's complete state
edge_cases.trigger: the view recomputes completion instead of reading state==complete
edge_cases.mitigation: render the tick only from the model's state==complete (done==total), keeping all completion logic in the model

workflow.action: Record the owner's calendar brief verbatim and separate open points
workflow.description: Reproduce the binding requirement table and list the owner-unresolved open points as such
workflow.gate: every stated element is tagged [FACT - owner brief] and the three open points are listed as owner-unresolved, not answered

workflow.action: Derive the per-day data model and percentage formula
workflow.description: Define {date, tasks_total, tasks_done, weight_done?, pct, state} with pct = floor((done/total)*20)*5 and the 21-state enumeration
workflow.gate: the 21 states, the pct formula and the tasks_total==0 guard are stated

workflow.action: Fix the floor-rounding rule and the tick invariant
workflow.description: Floor to the 5% grid so '100'/tick require done==total, tagging the estimate because the owner left direction open
workflow.gate: a test asserts done<total never yields pct==100 or state==complete and done==total yields the tick

workflow.description: White empty box with day number; a single green fill proportional to floored pct; view reads the model
workflow.gate: empty renders white with day number, partial renders one green fill proportional to floored pct, view computes nothing beyond reading pct/state

workflow.action: Decide or defer the task-weighting denominator
workflow.description: State unweighted count as the literal reading and weighting as an owner-unresolved build option behind the model interface
workflow.gate: the chosen denominator is documented with rationale and switching is shown to touch only the denominator

workflow.action: Specify the tick and the 5%-step partial numeral
workflow.description: Tick at state==complete; partial numeral is the floored pct in 5..95, agreeing with the fill
workflow.gate: the tick renders iff state==complete and the numeral equals the floored pct (5..95) matching the fill

workflow.action: Lay out the one-week and one-month views
workflow.description: Two box-per-day grids with identical per-box semantics; month view uses fill as primary cue
workflow.gate: a given day renders identically in both views and the month grid keeps the fill legible

workflow.action: Decide the past-day policy and the course-level metric
workflow.description: Name freeze-vs-gray as an owner-unresolved decision; derive a distinct course mastery % kept separate from day effort
workflow.gate: the past-day options are documented and applied consistently, and the course % is sourced from mastery and shown separate from day effort

workflow.action: Ground the design in prior art
workflow.description: Contrast GitHub's relative-colour heatmap and cite the Anki Review Heatmap SRS precedent with fetch grades
workflow.gate: GitHub's recalibrating quartile scale and the Anki add-on are stated with fetch-grade caveats and the absolute-vs-relative difference is justified

workflow.description: Plot upcoming scheduled burden in a style distinct from actual completion, flagged as an additive recommendation
workflow.gate: forecast state is visually distinct from completion, cannot show the tick, and is marked a recommendation not an owner requirement

workflow.action: Ground the psychology and build the guardrail posture
workflow.description: Cite goal-gradient (Kivetz 2006), habit horizon (Lally 2010), streak+freeze (Duolingo), and the overjustification/streak-anxiety guardrails
workflow.gate: each finding is cited with its correct grade and the guardrail posture (informational feedback, streak-with-freeze, non-punitive backlog) is stated

workflow.action: Compose the owner-faithful enforceable build spec
workflow.description: Enumerate the day-box, views, course metric, forecast and guardrails; mark open points as build-time decisions
workflow.gate: the spec enumerates every component, keeps the three open points as build-time decisions, and a fidelity check confirms every stated owner semantic is preserved

priority_rationale: The owner-fidelity brief and the derived day-box data model come first because every render, view and metric is a function of the owner's verbatim spec and the {date, tasks, pct, state} object; the floor-rounding rule, fill render, tick and 5%-step numeral next, because they are the render primitives and the correctness invariant (display-100 <=> tick <=> truly complete) that the whole visual depends on; the week/month views, past-day policy, course-level metric and effort-vs-mastery separation then apply those primitives across the surfaces the owner named while keeping effort and mastery distinct; the prior-art grounding (GitHub heatmap, Anki add-on, future-load) and the psychology (goal-gradient, habit horizon, streak, and the overjustification/streak-anxiety guardrails) justify and bound the design; and the guardrail synthesis and the owner-faithful go-spec come last because they compose every upstream output into one enforceable, fidelity-checked build spec.

dominance_rules.rationale: the brief is binding product truth, not a proposal to redesign
dominance_rules.trigger: a design choice would change a stated owner semantic (white empty, green download-fill, tick at 100, 5%-increment percentage)
dominance_rules.action: preserve the owner's semantic and only resolve genuinely unspecified points, recording those as build-time decisions

dominance_rules.rule: The floor-rounding invariant dominates any generosity tweak
dominance_rules.rationale: the tick is the owner's distinguished terminal state and must mean true completion
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal rounds up or to nearest so a sub-100 day could show 100 or the tick
dominance_rules.action: floor to the 5% grid so display-100 and the tick require done==total; handle near-top generosity in copy, not rounding

dominance_rules.rationale: expected tangible rewards can undermine intrinsic motivation (Deci/Koestner/Ryan 1999; Lepper 1973) while informational feedback does not
dominance_rules.trigger: a gamification element adds points/prizes/currency for studying
dominance_rules.action: keep the fill/tick/percentage as informational feedback and reject the tangible-reward economy

dominance_rules.rule: Streak-with-freeze dominates a bare reset-on-miss streak
dominance_rules.rationale: loss-aversion power makes an unprotected broken streak a quit risk
dominance_rules.trigger: a streak is specified without a freeze/repair or a secondary long-horizon metric
dominance_rules.action: add a pre-equipped freeze/repair and a secondary metric a single miss cannot zero, and keep the backlog non-punitive

dominance_rules.rule: The mastery source dominates for course progress
dominance_rules.rationale: course progress must answer 'how much have I mastered', not 'how much did I do today'
dominance_rules.trigger: course-level progress is computed from daily task completion
dominance_rules.action: derive the course percentage from the learner/mastery model and keep it separate from day-box effort

dominance_rules.rule: The single model pct dominates any per-encoding recomputation
dominance_rules.rationale: the numeral, fill and tick must never disagree
dominance_rules.trigger: the fill, numeral or tick is computed separately from the model's pct/state
dominance_rules.action: drive every encoding from the one model value and render the tick only from state==complete

dominance_rules.rule: Absolute fill-height completion dominates relative-colour encoding
dominance_rules.rationale: each study day has a defined denominator, so absolute completion is more meaningful than a rank against the user's busiest days
dominance_rules.trigger: a GitHub-style relative-colour quartile scale is proposed for the study calendar
dominance_rules.action: use the owner's absolute fill height + numeral; reserve relative colour for a true volume view only if explicitly requested

dominance_rules.rule: Non-punitive scheduling dominates any streak/past-day display choice
dominance_rules.rationale: a display decision must never degrade the actual spaced-repetition backlog
dominance_rules.trigger: a broken streak or a grayed past day would de-prioritize or hide backlog tasks
dominance_rules.action: keep the display choice cosmetic and leave the SRS backlog and scheduling quality untouched

dominance_rules.rule: Vendor engagement claims are dominated by their attribution
dominance_rules.rationale: Duolingo's 2.4x is the vendor's own number, not independent evidence
dominance_rules.trigger: a vendor engagement statistic is cited to justify a design
dominance_rules.action: carry the figure explicitly as the vendor's claim and do not treat it as independent proof

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the owner's brief verbatim and mark open points before any design work
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silently redesigning a stated owner semantic or inventing an answer to an unspecified point and having to unwind it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put the floor-rounding tick invariant in the data model with a test from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a false tick on a sub-100 day surfacing after the render is built and needing a rounding rewrite

anti_rework_rules.rule: Drive the fill, numeral and tick from one model pct/state value
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the numeral and fill disagreeing and a later refactor to unify the encodings

anti_rework_rules.rule: Separate day-effort and course-mastery metrics with distinct inputs and labels up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a conflated progress number that must be untangled after learners are confused

anti_rework_rules.rule: Specify the streak as streak-with-freeze plus a secondary metric when it is first designed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a bare reset-on-miss streak shipping and causing quit-after-break churn that a redesign must fix

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the informational-feedback-not-reward posture before adding any gamification element
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a points/prizes economy being built and then removed after it undermines intrinsic motivation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose one past-day policy and apply it identically across week and month views
anti_rework_rules.prevents: inconsistent past-day rendering between views that must be reconciled later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Render forecast future-load in a style that can never show the tick from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: forecast boxes being mistaken for completed days and a rework to distinguish the states

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner resolves an open point (rounding direction, past-day freeze-vs-gray, or task weighting)
iteration_protocol.action: replace the tagged recommendation with the owner's decision and re-run the day-box and go-spec acceptance tests

iteration_protocol.trigger: engagement data for this system shows the streak causing quit-after-break churn
iteration_protocol.action: strengthen the freeze/repair and secondary-metric guardrails and re-check the guardrail posture

iteration_protocol.trigger: the official GitHub contributions doc or the AnkiWeb listing becomes fetchable and revises the prior-art detail
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the fetch grade and correct any quartile/feature specifics in the prior-art grounding

iteration_protocol.trigger: the learner/mastery model changes how course mastery is scored
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the course-level percentage and re-verify the effort-vs-mastery separation

iteration_protocol.trigger: month-view legibility testing fails for the 5%-step numeral in small cells
iteration_protocol.action: shift the month view to fill-as-primary with numeral-on-inspection and re-test both views for identical semantics

iteration_protocol.trigger: a proposal to add points/badges/currency for studying is raised
iteration_protocol.action: apply the overjustification guardrail and the composed posture to accept or reject the element

iteration_protocol.trigger: task-duration data shows heterogeneity large enough to distort the unweighted percentage
iteration_protocol.action: reconsider the weighted-vs-unweighted denominator behind the model interface and update the day-box
